description:
FOUND s500a (Opus, 2026-09-30) by the #2085 boundary probes (scratch/s500a/probes/hashctor3.pl rows 2 and 9).  PRE-EXISTING on main 558cc5a0 (base and tree identical).  Probed vs perl 5.40.3:

    sub g { map { $_ => 1 } @_ }   my @l = qw(a b);
    print scalar(@{ [ { g(@l) } ] }), "\n";          perl 1      PCL 4     <-- SILENT WRONG
    print join(",", sort { { $a <=> $b } } (3,1,2));  perl 3,2,1  PCL 1,2,3 (perl reads the inner {..} as an anon HASH; rare, recorded for completeness)

The first is the SIBLING of #2085 in the ARRAY-CONSTRUCTOR position: inside `[ ... ]` a brace group in TERM position is an anonymous hash in perl (toke.c XTERM -> HASHBRACK); PPI hands it over as a Statement::Compound holding a bare Structure::Block (the same shape as #2085's `%{{ g(@l) }}`), and PCL lowers it as a bare BLOCK whose value (the flattened list a,1,b,1) is spliced into the array.  #2085 (s500a) taught the ONE classifier `Pl::PExpr::_block_is_hash_constructor($block, $pos)` a 'deref' position; this is a second position for the same classifier ('term' inside `[...]`, a function's argument list, a list), and its boundary needs its own probe table (perl's intuit for `{` at XSTATE vs XTERM: `[ { g() } ]`, `f({ g() })`, `( { g() } )`, `return { g() }` -- measure which PPI already makes a Constructor first).
The sort row: perl parses the inner `{ $a <=> $b }` of a sort block as a hash too (the comparator returns a hash ref -> numeric address); a program that relies on it is unlikely; do NOT widen the sort-body classifier for it without a population count.
subject: SILENT WRONG, the #2085 sibling in TERM position: `[ { g(@l) } ]` builds a 4-element array (the brace group lowered as a bare BLOCK whose list is spliced) where perl builds ONE anon hash -- PPI hands a Statement::Compound(bare Block); the classifier _block_is_hash_constructor knows the deref position since s500a, not the term position
